questions.q: What did the Doctor do when he first got back to his own country, before going home?
choices: He went straight to the sailor to return the boat
He traveled to country-fairs with the pushmi-pullyu
He wrote a big new book about all the animals of Africa
He visited the King to tell him about the pirates
questions.evidence: First he went traveling through the land with the pushmi-pullyu in a gipsy-wagon

questions.q: Why did Dab-Dab keep scolding the Doctor at the fairs?
choices: He let children in for nothing when she wasn't looking
He spent all the sixpences on candy and toys for the children
He forgot to feed the pushmi-pullyu every day
He fell asleep in his chair in front of the wagon
questions.evidence: he would let the children in for nothing when she wasn't looking

questions.q: What did the Doctor always say when circus-men wanted to buy the pushmi-pullyu?
choices: Yes, but only if they gave the animal a big green garden to live in
No, because he was too shy to be seen
Yes, once he was home safe in Puddleby
No, because he should never be shut in a cage
questions.evidence: The pushmi-pullyu shall never be shut up in a cage

questions.q: How did the Doctor come back to Puddleby at the end?
choices: As a famous wizard
As a poor sailor
As a rich man
As a circus-man
questions.evidence: he came back to Puddleby a rich man

questions.q: Why did the Doctor buy another piano?
choices: To play songs for the animals
To put the white mice back in it
To give to the sailor's baby
To sell again at the country-fair
questions.evidence: he bought another piano and put the white mice back in it

questions.q: What did Gub-Gub do when they got back to the garden?
choices: Dug up the horseradish that had grown three feet high
Chased the rats out of the tool-shed by the wall
Rolled in the flower-beds where the hollyhocks grew
Ate up every one of the muffins that Dab-Dab was toasting for tea

questions.q: The Doctor said money "is a terrible nuisance." What is a "nuisance"?
choices: Something that makes you very happy
Something that is easy to lose
Something that you must give away to the poor
Something that bothers or troubles you
questions.evidence: Money," he said, "is a terrible nuisance

questions.q: What is this last chapter mostly about?
choices: The Doctor sets sail for Africa again to visit the monkeys and Polynesia
The Doctor sells the pushmi-pullyu to a circus and buys a new house
The Doctor comes home rich and happy, and his friends in Africa miss him
The Doctor and Jip dig up all the old bones that had been buried long ago
questions.evidence: I think he will--I guess he will--I hope he will!
